head_commit.message:
Fix engine liquidity estimates: eligibility needs both, and an exit after a missing bar uses the bars its windows hold (BH-2026-10-21-1, BH-2026-10-09-1) (#30)

* Require both liquidity estimates for eligibility and let exits use the latest known ones (BH-2026-10-21-1, BH-2026-10-09-1)

Decision-time eligibility checked the trailing ADV but not the trailing
volatility a fill needs, so a name listed adv_window sessions earlier got
weight and its order was rejected no_liquidity_estimate (BH-2026-10-21-1).
A single missing bar left a held name's trailing windows incomplete for
adv_window sessions, so every sell was rejected no_liquidity_estimate
while the other targets were sized on equity that still held it, and
gross exposure exceeded gross_leverage (BH-2026-10-09-1).

Eligibility now also requires a finite volatility estimate, and orders
use the latest estimates known at their decision. Targets only name
eligible instruments, so only the exit of a name whose windows a missing
bar interrupted uses older estimates. The docs say when a missing bar can
still block an exit: when the fill date itself has no bar.

TODO gains REVIEW-23 (this fix) and REVIEW-24 to REVIEW-26 for the open
medium bug-hunt findings that had no item yet (REVIEW-19 to REVIEW-22 are
taken by open pull requests #26 and #27).

* Pin eligibility and exit costs in tests, correct the replay figures, record the exits that still cannot trade (review round 3)

- Tests: A is ineligible at the decisions whose ADV window the gap
  interrupts and eligible again once it is complete; the unblocked exit
  pays impact on the volatility known at its decision, never a later one.
- README and HISTORICAL_BASELINE: the 2026-10-07 replay on this code gives
  net CAGR -5.67% and max drawdown 61.6% (GEV is no longer eligible at the
  2024-04-24 decision).
- strategy-evaluation README: eligibility also needs a finite score and no
  delisting settlement; the exit is still rejected without a fill-date bar
  or with a zero ADV, and the participation cap can make it partial.
- TODO REVIEW-27: exits that still cannot trade (zero ADV, multi-session
  halt) leave gross exposure above gross_leverage; needs a decision.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Size and price an interrupted exit on the bars its windows hold (review round 5)

The fallback for an exit whose trailing windows a missing bar interrupted
was the last complete estimate, however old. After a halt longer than
adv_window it capped the first sales by the volume from before the halt:
in the reviewer's probe A sold $50M a session while trading $1M, and the
fills recorded a participation of 0.05.

The exit now uses the bars and daily returns its windows still hold (at
least one bar and two returns); every other order still uses the complete
windows that eligibility requires. A halt now leaves the exit rejected
until its windows hold a bar and two returns (REVIEW-27).

- Tests: the exit after a halt is capped by the volume traded since; an
  exit decided on a session with a close but an incomplete window fills
  with participation measured on the bars it holds; eligibility waits for
  the longer of the two windows; the earlier exit tests now expect the
  in-window estimates.
- README: 342 more name-decisions than the earlier runs (343 added by
  REVIEW-13, one dropped by REVIEW-23); HISTORICAL_BASELINE notes the 5%
  tails' reason counts (717 instead of 716 of 751 decisions).
- TODO REVIEW-27 adds exits the participation cap fills only in part and
  the sessions after a halt.

* Pin in-window exit estimates and delayed fills in tests; qualify the exit docs (review round 6)

- Tests: an exit whose ADV window holds one bar fills on that bar; the
  exit decided on a session with a close prices its impact on the returns
  inside its window, none spanning the gap; a fill with delay 2 uses the
  ADV known at its decision.
- README, strategy-evaluation README, TODO REVIEW-23 and REVIEW-27: a
  missing bar still blocks the exit when a window is too short to hold a
  bar or two returns without it (adv_window 1, vol_window below 4); the
  cap after a halt shorter than adv_window still reflects bars from before
  the halt, as a complete window does after volume falls.
- engine.py comment: the volatility stays undefined for vol_window + 1
  sessions after a missing bar.

* Let an exit fall back on a window's last complete estimate when the window is too short (BH-2026-10-09-1)

Re-running the bug hunt's own reproduction of BH-2026-10-09-1 on 6cc6c2b
still failed: it uses vol_window 2, and a missing bar removes two daily
returns, so for three sessions the window held fewer than the two returns
an in-window volatility needs and the exit was rejected
no_liquidity_estimate (gross 1.33). adv_window 1 had the same gap for the
ADV. 6808bcf had moved its own test from vol_window 2 to 3 instead.

A window too short to hold a bar or two returns without the missing one
now falls back on its last complete estimate, if that is at most one
window old (adv_window sessions for the ADV, vol_window + 1 for the
volatility, which a single gap leaves undefined that long). A longer halt
still leaves the exit rejected until the windows hold a bar and two
returns measured after it.

- Tests: the missing-bar test is back on vol_window 2, as in the bug
  hunt's reproduction; a single missing bar never blocks the exit for
  windows (1, 2), (2, 2), (5, 2), (5, 3) and (3, 8) with the decision 0
  to 3 sessions after it; the halt test also runs with adv_window 2 and
  vol_window 20, so an unbounded ADV fallback fails it.
- Docs: README, strategy-evaluation README, ExecutionConfig docstring,
  TODO REVIEW-23 and REVIEW-27.

* Pin the ADV fallback's age limit with a halt one session longer than adv_window

A third halt case (adv_window 2, no bars on sessions 32 to 34): the last
complete ADV, from session 31, is one session older than the limit, so the
sale decided on session 34 is rejected instead of capped by the volume
from before the halt. A limit of adv_window + 1 now fails the test.

* Limit the exit fallback to the session just before a single gap (review round 7)

Round 7 found that the fallback on a window's last complete estimate,
allowed up to one window old, also fired after halts: at the session a
halt emptied the ADV window, the last complete ADV was exactly adv_window
sessions old, so a sale decided there filled on the first bar after the
halt, capped by the volume from before it (50 times that session's dollar
volume with windows 5/5 and delay 0, or 20/20 and delay 1). The docs said
such a sale is rejected.

The fallback now reaches back at most one session for the ADV and three
for the volatility, exactly what a single missing bar needs with
adv_window 1 or vol_window 2 or 3. Once a halt has emptied a window, the
fallback cannot reach the trading before it.

- Tests: halts as long as the window at delay 0 and one longer at delay 1
  (both failed before), a delayed sale whose participation uses the ADV
  known at its decision, and the two fallback age limits (an ADV two
  sessions old and a volatility four sessions old are not used).
- Docs: strategy-evaluation README, ExecutionConfig docstring, README,
  TODO REVIEW-23 and REVIEW-27 (which now also names two missing bars
  close together with vol_window below 4).

* Correct the exit fallback's documented limits (review round 8)

The three-session volatility fallback leaves an exit after two missing bars
a few sessions apart blocked up to vol_window 5 (7 for three bars), not
only below 4, and with adv_window 1 and a delay a sale decided on a halt's
first session can still fill after the halt at the pre-halt volume. Say so
in the engine comment, the strategy-evaluation README and REVIEW-27.

* Let an exit's volatility fall back up to vol_window + 1 sessions (checkpoint decision)

Review round 8 found that the three-session volatility fallback from
15ae0ed blocks an exit after two missing bars two or three sessions apart
with vol_window 4 or 5, so gross exposure again exceeded gross_leverage.
The volatility only prices a sale's impact, so it may fall back on the
estimate from just before the gap for up to vol_window + 1 sessions, as
before 15ae0ed. The ADV, which caps the sale, keeps its one-session limit
from round 7. The requester chose this at the checkpoint on 2026-10-26.

Two missing bars now block an exit only with vol_window 2 or 3, three
only up to 5 (REVIEW-27, which also records the requester's decision to
size the other targets net of an unsold position).

* Pin the exit volatility fallback for every vol_window and fix its wording (review round 9)

Round 9 (Opus, xhigh, helper) found no defect in c3238d6 and three
optional items, fixed here:

- R9-1: the engine comment said a few missing bars close together never
  block an exit and framed the volatility fallback as serving only short
  windows. It serves any window left with fewer than two returns, for up
  to vol_window + 1 sessions; two missing bars still block it with a
  vol_window up to 3, three up to 5 (as the README says). REVIEW-23 now
  says the same.
- R9-2: the vol_window + 1 limit was pinned only for vol_window 4 and 5.
  New cases: two missing bars with vol_window 3, and a halt of
  vol_window sessions with vol_window 6, 8 and 11. They kill the two
  surviving mutants (limit 3 when vol_window <= 3, limit vol_window when
  vol_window >= 6).
- R9-3: REVIEW-27 read as if adv_window 1 needed two zero-volume
  sessions to block an exit; one does, two are needed only for missing
  bars.
